newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks up 3.00 pct in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks up 3.00 pct in late trade.

text.p: Taiwan's trendsetting financials and electronics surged further in late Friday trade, pushing the share index up sharply into seven-year intraday high range, brokers said.
With 55 minutes left, at 0305 GMT, the index was up 259.05 points or 3.00 percent at 8,895.34, surpassing a seven-year intraday high of 8,827.88 set on Thursday.
Turnover was an extremely heavy T$140 billion.
Financials had surged 4.85 percent and electronics 4.23 percent -- a rare confluence of the heavily weighted and usually contrarian sectors that brokers dubbed "dual mainstreaming".
"The two most heavily weighted sectors are rising at the same time, indicating a big bullish trend has emerged," said HSBC James Capel research manager Alex Chen.
Financials account for some 20 percent of the market's weighting, while electronics represent 12 percent, Chen said.
"The financials' surge was especially important as it's a signal the government wants the market to be bullish," he said, noting that probable state intervention was apparent.
